summary: My declared slot was attention microarchitecture at fixed FLOPs, and it produced one keeper and two clean negatives. The keeper: shrinking the sliding window of the S layers from seq/2 to seq/4 (short_window = long_window // 4, a one-character change) is worth about -0.0012 at d=512 and -0.0017 at d=768, and it is now bracketed on both sides at the identical d=768 shape (all-L 0.983388 > seq/2 0.981817 > seq/4 0.980071), so it is a monotone effect rather than noise. The negatives: HEAD_DIM is a sharp optimum at 128 -- both 64 (1.003 vs 0.997) and 256 (0.9897 vs 0.9852) lose about 0.005 -- and gated attention (per-head sigmoid gate on the attention output, zero-init) is a wash for 4 lines, so I removed it. I also measured that shrinking the window buys no wall-clock at all (MFU falls proportionally; attention here is launch/memory-bound, not FLOP-bound), so the gain is purely a modelling gain. My best run combines the collective findings -- TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE 2**18 with grad_accum 1, and width d=768 at depth 8 -- with my window change, for 0.980071, the best in the cell, at four changed constants and zero added code. One run of mine was wasted: I used DEVICE_BATCH_SIZE=64 to fit d=896 in VRAM, and peers concurrently showed that splitting the micro-batch costs ~0.05 bpb because grad_accum 2 roughly halves the steps in a fixed 5 minutes; d=896 is past the width optimum anyway. Next I would try short_window = seq/8 (256) on 627aeb7, since the window trend has not turned over, and then re-tune MATRIX_LR at d=768, since every LR retune so far was done at d=512.
